questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Local State Management”?
options: Local State Management means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Local State Management removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Local State Management should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Local State Management helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Local State Management helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Local State Management is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Component properties” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Component properties” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Component properties” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Component properties” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Component properties” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Component properties” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Component properties” under Local State Management. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Local State Management”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
